title: Introduce CUTLASS version shim + CI gating to isolate kernel ABI changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Frequent CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA dependency bumps cause intermittent production regressions (kernel symbol mismatches, increased cold-start latency, and sporadic OOMs) and long rollbacks. Root cause analysis across multiple incidents shows we lack a lightweight runtime shim and CI gating that can validate multiple CUTLASS versions side-by-side and isolate ABI changes before they reach runtime.

Goal: Build an in-process CUTLASS version shim and CI test matrix that: (1) loads and validates multiple CUTLASS runtime artifacts without requiring full image rebuilds; (2) exercises a small set of critical kernels and quant paths for regression detection; (3) provides automatic telemetry and an automated rollback hook when regressions are detected in canary/dedicated fleets.

Scope:
- Runtime component: a minimal shim library that abstracts kernel lookup + symbol versioning and exposes a deterministic probe and validation API. The shim should support loading two CUTLASS variants concurrently (primary and fallback) and expose a metrics surface for probe latency and mismatch rates.
- CI/validation: expand nightly matrix to include the shim with CUTLASS X.Y and X.Y+1 artifacts; add microbench harness (short sequences, KV cache warmed/unwarmed) that runs in <10 minutes per variant; fail PRs on regression thresholds.
- Rollout plan: integrate with canary jobs (Dedicated) with automatic circuit-breaker that falls back to pinned runtime on high error/latency. Document rollback playbook.

Non-goals: full multi-version runtime for all libraries (we target CUTLASS first, then Triton kernels in follow-up). This ticket does not include on-prem installer changes (handled in Private roadmap).
acceptance_criteria: Shim library can load and enumerate symbols from two CUTLASS shared objects and return a deterministic compatibility report.
CI matrix includes at least three CUTLASS version pairs and will fail PRs when kernel microbench latency regresses >10% or error rate increases >1% on test harness.
Canary pipeline integrates shim health check and triggers automatic fallback when regressions cross thresholds; playbook for manual rollback is written and approved.
Perf dashboard shows baseline vs candidate CUTLASS run metrics (p50/p95 latency, memory high-water, kernel mismatch count) for each canary deployment.
Documentation and runbook published: confluence link + playbook steps for on-call and release engineers.

2025-12-07 - Rodrigo Silva: Prototype landed in branch feature/shim-proto. Early findings: dlopen order matters across CUDA versions; added deterministic loader ordering and timestamped artifact naming convention. See PR #6137.
